articles.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. to Start Colts' Preseason Finale amid NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. will get one last chance to impress potential trade suitors later this week.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. will get one last chance to impress potential trade suitors later this week.

Per ESPN's Stephen Holder , Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced on Tuesday that Richardson will be the starting quarterback for the team's preseason finale against the Detroit Lions on Saturday.

Holder added that the Colts' starters will likely play "a series or two," though quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor will remain on the sidelines. Jones is still targeting a Week 1 return as he recovers from a torn Achilles.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Richardson started Indianapolis' preseason opener against the New England Patriots but played the second half in last week's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Across the two appearances, he completed 14 of his 23 passes for 169 yards and an interception while also rushing for 68 yards and one touchdown.

The No. 4 pick in the 2023 draft should be motivated to go out with a bang on Saturday against the Lions. Richardson requested to be traded this offseason, but Colts general manager Chris Ballard told reporters last month that the team is "not going to give him away."

Despite the lackluster start to his career and the ongoing trade rumors, Richardson expressed optimism that he would be able to produce for the Colts if they retain him and he has to step in for Jones.

"I'm just looking forward to helping the team," Richardson told Holder . "They truly believe that I still have a chance to be on this squad, and I love that. I just want to be able to contribute."

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Dynasty Rankings, Cheat Sheet and League Names
articles.summary: While re-draft fantasy football leagues treat each NFL season as their own, unique stories, dynasty leagues are different.
articles.body:
While re-draft fantasy football leagues treat each NFL season as their own, unique stories, dynasty leagues are different.

In a dynasty format, NFL campaigns become mere chapters of a years-long (or, for the real sickos like myself, decades-long) journey.

As such, everything needs adjusting—rankings, position values, draft approaches and even the general character of the league as conveyed through its name. If you're a dynasty-drafter preparing for the upcoming season, we're here to help with overall dynasty rankings, cheat sheet positional breakdowns and finally tips for crafting the right league name.

What's in a name? Well, for fantasy football leagues, quite a bit actually. Or plenty if you craft the right one, at least.

Step one is nailing down the tone and the theme. Do you want something serious and official sounding, or are you going for a chuckle? Then, figure out if you're going for a general, perhaps openly inviting name—newcomers won't feel like they're missing a joke if they're joining the Waiver Warriors or Armchair Experts, for instance—or if you want something more specific. If specifics are the aim, look for something you share, like a location and maybe a specific NFL allegiance, for instance. Say you're all Green Bay Packers fans, then maybe collectively you're the Lambeau Leapers Collective (LLC, for short).

Or maybe you all came together as fans of movies, video games or even non-football sports. If you're a bunch of Marvel fans, maybe the league is as simple as The Multiverse. For old-school gamers, you might be the Tecmo Bowl All-Stars. If baseball is a shared first love, maybe it's The Extra Innings Endzone.

Only you, of course, know the particulars with your league mates, so you'll know better than us what actually works best. But, honestly, give this some real thought. It might seem like such an afterthought when putting a league together, but it can be a legitimate point of pride. And if it gives your league an edge over others played in by fellow managers, that can lead to a more eventful and therefore enjoyable experience.

articles.title: Brian Thomas Jr. Suffers Shoulder Injury at Practice, Status Updated by Jaguars' Liam Coen
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen offered an update on the shoulder injury that led to wideout Brian Thomas Jr. missing the remainder of Tuesday's practice.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen offered an update on the shoulder injury that led to wideout Brian Thomas Jr. missing the remainder of Tuesday's practice.

"I think it's alright," he told reporters . "Just came down on his shoulder. Holding him out was smart, keep him out and then get him going for Cleveland."

There are plenty of questions regarding Thomas heading into the 2026 season.

After an epic rookie campaign in 2024 (87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns), big things were expected last season. But as any fantasy football enthusiast could tell you, Thomas instead struggled, managing just 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns across 14 games.

One explanation was that the system Coen and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski brought with them in 2025 didn't suit Thomas' skill set as much as the one employed by head coach Doug Pederson and offensive coordinator Press Taylor in 2024. The Jaguars eventually adjusted his role in the offense, employing him more on the outside later in the season, which seemed to help.

"Just growing, getting better with the offense," Thomas told reporters in February. "It took a little time, but yeah, for sure, I definitely think [I hit a stride]... Just got more comfortable and just was able to go out there and play a little bit more."

Thomas also battled some injury and drop issues during the season, and at times he and quarterback Trevor Lawrence didn't seem to quite be on the same page. But he's still expected to be a major part of the offense in 2026.

The Jaguars have a lot of options in the passing game, however, are pretty loaded at the position. In Thomas, Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter, the Jags have one of the deepest wideout groups in the sport.

But a healthy and revitalized Thomas makes the Jags all the more dynamic. That will make this latest shoulder injury one to monitor heading into a Week 1 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: Predicting When Malik Nabers, More Injured NFL Stars Will Make 2026 NFL Debut
articles.summary: The start of the 2026 NFL season is only a few short weeks away, but there won't be a full compliment of stars available when teams take the field in Week 1. Several of the league's top names are still working their way back from injuries picked up both last year and during the offseason.
articles.body:
The start of the 2026 NFL season is only a few short weeks away, but there won't be a full compliment of stars available when teams take the field in Week 1. Several of the league's top names are still working their way back from injuries picked up both last year and during the offseason.

While some of these marquee players have begun practicing in recent weeks, others have yet to be cleared and could be sidelined for an extensive stretch. Most teams have been understandably vague when discussing timelines for potential returns, leaving fans to sift through clues and guess when these headliners will return.

With that in mind, let's highlight some of the NFL's biggest stars who still don't have a concrete timetable to return from a significant injury and predict when they will make their 2026 debut.

George Kittle remains an integral piece of the San Francisco 49ers' offensive plans, but the team has been preparing to go without their veteran tight end and leader for a stretch due to the torn Achilles he suffered back in January. That absence isn't likely to linger beyond the first month of the 2026 NFL season, however, as Kittle has been activated off the PUP list and is trending towards a September return.

The 49ers announced the move on Sunday, with Kittle sitting out team drills but still suiting up in full pads and easing into things with individual work. Had the nine-year veteran remained on the PUP list through cutdown day on August 30, he would have needed to miss the first four games at a minimum.

Kittle has long maintained that he wanted to be ready for San Francisco's much-anticipated opener against the rival Los Angeles Rams, set to take place in Melbourne, Australia on September 11. He's kept that as his desired return date, but recently admitted missing one game during the grind of a long season won't be too devastating.

"I want to play in every football game that I possibly can play in but I'm also aware it's an 18-week season," Kittle said earlier this month (via ESPN's Nick Wagoner ). "If you miss Week 1 and you're playing Week 2, hey, it is what it is. I'm just going to keep that as my goal and then we'll adjust from there if we need to."

Even if he's medically cleared, given the unconventional preparations and lengthy travel involved with San Francisco's opening contest—the team plans to arrive in Australia over a week before kickoff to help players and staff acclimate to a 17-hour time difference—it would make sense for Kittle to delay his return slightly.

The team will settle back into a conventional routine after returning stateside, benefitting from a three-game homestand that begins with a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. If he ends up sitting out Week 1, expect Kittle to make his 2026 debut during this contest.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 2 vs. Miami Dolphins

The Arizona Cardinals went all-in on overhauling a lackluster and injury-prone running back platoon by selecting Jeremiyah Love at No. 3 overall in the 2026 NFL draft. While Love is still expected to be the focal point of the rebuilding program's offense, his chances of jumping out to a fast start took a major hit when he suffered a high-ankle sprain during his first preseason outing.

Love's injury ended what was a promising 11-carry, 58-yard debut on a sour note. Shortly after the contest ended, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that that the Notre Dame product was likely going to be held out the remainder of the preseason with the hopes of getting healthy in time for the regular season opener on September 13.

It seems that the Cardinals are sticking to the plan Schefter initially reported. Arizona Sports' Tyler Drake provided an update on Love, stating he's making "steady progress" in his recovery but will remain out of practice this week. The Cardinals are slated to take on the Green Bay Packers in the preseason finale on Friday, which follows a joint practice session on Wednesday.

With head coach Mike LaFleur confirming that Love won't be suiting up for any activity this week, it's fair to wonder whether the rising star will actually be ready by Week 1.

The Cardinals would be wise to take an extremely cautious approach with a player set to be a building block for years to come, especially with the amount of depth they've accumulated in the backfield. With incumbent James Conner and free-agent pickup Tyler Allgeier in the mix, Arizona doesn't need to rush the rookie into action if he's not fully healthy.

Given the strength of this platoon coupled with the four-week timetable for recovery from this type of injury, it isn't worth pushing Love into the lineup for Week 1 if he's not 100 percent. Missing an entire week of practice won't help the rookie's case either, so it's more reasonable to expect him to make his NFL debut when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks come to town in Week 2.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks

Malik Nabers' absence for much of the offseason has been one of the more enigmatic stories swirling around head coach John Harbaugh's inaugural season with the New York Giants.

The superstar wideout went down with a severe knee injury in late-September of last year and underwent surgery for the issue approximately one month later. Nabers also had another procedure done earlier this year to clear out scar tissue and address stiffness issues. He only recently returned to practice, initially wearing a no-contact red jersey before shedding it and going on to participate in several 11-on-11 drills earlier this week.

While that training camp activity seems to indicate that Nabers will be ready to go when the G-Men open their 2026 NFL season against the Dallas Cowboys on September 13, Harbaugh only hinted it would be "reasonable to assume" the receiver will be active.

"The only thing I know more than you guys know is what the doctors and trainers tell me as far as his rehab," Harbaugh said Monday , ". And that is he's doing well. He's doing well with that. He's strong, in a good place. How he gets through practice, how ready he is to play and protect himself is really based on practice."

Nabers made one impressive grab during Monday's practice session but also had a drop and was whistled for a false start. While those moments aren't ideal, it's tough to envision the 2024 Pro Bowler failing to make a positive impact upon his much-anticipated return. New York's receiving corps has a good mix of solid veterans and promising young pieces, but none have the ceiling a healthy Nabers provides.

If he's medically cleared and able, Nabers will suit up and play against the Cowboys. He's far too important to Big Blue's 2026 chances to miss any time he's healthy enough to see.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 1 vs. Dallas Cowboys

One of the Indianapolis Colts' biggest offseason moves was to issue a massive contract extension to burgeoning wideout Alec Pierce. While the team paid Pierce on the heels of his best season yet—a 47-catch, 1,003-yard, six-touchdown effort—there are expectations for an expanded role attached to the four-year, $114 million deal.

Considering Pierce has yet to suit up for a training camp practice, the chances of the four-year veteran quickly adapting to this larger role look bleaker than ever. The wideout has been plagued by a lingering ankle injury since late in the 2024 season, attempting to treat the issue with a platelet-rich plasma injection early in the offseason before opting for surgery.

Back in June, Pierce spoke about how the ankle progressed last year and seemed happy to finally have it addressed.

"It definitely got a little bit worse as the (2025) season went," Pierce said. "Probably the last month I'd say I was kind of struggling – (it) affected practice, I'd taken some days off. I'm glad they figured out what the issue was and we were able to fix it."

Pierce's recovery has been slow, as he underwent the procedure in the spring and has since missed all of OTAs and training camp. The Colts initially expected him back in early-August, as Rotowire's Ian Hartitz pointed out that it's now been a month since the club projected a one-to-two week timeline for his return.

According to The Athletic's James Boyd , head coach Shane Steichen confirmed that Pierce wouldn't be back in action on Tuesday, but is still hopeful the wideout can suit up at some point during the coming week.

With little in the way of proven weapons outside of Josh Downs and aging free-agent pickup Keenan Allen to lean on during Pierce's absence, the Colts need Pierce to get back on the field and pick up his new role as soon as possible. Even if Pierce doesn't get many practice reps under his belt, expect Steichen—likely coaching for his job in 2026—to thrust the wideout into action and have him learn on the fly.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 1 vs. Baltimore Ravens

The New Orleans Saints' Jordyn Tyson is set to miss extensive time after going down with a hamstring issue during a joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this month.

Tyson is one of the more promising pass-catchers to enter the league in years, but his selection at No. 8 overall raised eyebrows due to health-related red flags surrounding the prospect. The Arizona State product missed a myriad of games at the previous level, including 11 contests stemming from an ACL tear and three games last season with a hamstring strain.

While Tyson is undeniably tough—notably gritting through multiple hamstring issues to lead Arizona State with 10 catches, 105 yards and a score in a win over Texas Tech last October—he's set to miss approximately half of his rookie season while recovering from his latest injury.

Per ESPN's Katherine Terell , the hamstring injury that Tyson suffered while landing awkwardly after a catch is different in nature to the one that plagued him during his final collegiate season. Head coach Kellen Moore revealed that the previous injury also didn't play a role in causing or worsening the current one.

Prior to the injury, Tyson had been a near-full participant in practices—only avoiding one-on-one drills against defensive backs in an effort to preserve his health and get him up to full strength for his rookie campaign.

With Tyson on the shelf until approximately mid-October at a minimum, a Week 5 return at home against the Minnesota Vikings would be the earliest reasonably expect him back. New Orleans' scheduling isn't too favorable for this target date, however, as the team visits the New York Giants in Week 6 and travels all the way to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7 before a Week 8 bye.

Rather than rush Tyson back, have him travel to Europe and chance yet another injury to a player with incredible upside, it would behoove the Saints to keep their prized rookie on ice until a Week 9 bout against the Cleveland Browns at the Superdome.

Projected 2026 Debut: Week 9 vs. Cleveland Browns

articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.

Monken also said that Deshaun Watson was the clear frontrunner for the starting position in the spring but Sanders made it a competition with his play over the summer.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Watson was officially, and somewhat shockingly , named the team's starter on Monday.

Neither Watson or Sanders were exactly brilliant during the first two preseason games:

But history suggests that Watson has little room for growth. Since joining the Browns in 2022 he's thrown for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns and 12 interceptions across 19 games, taking 70 sacks while completing 61.2 percent of his passes. The Browns are 9-10 in his starts.

Sanders is more of an unknown, though his rookie season was rough after he threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games (seven starts), taking 23 sacks while completing just 56.6 percent of his passes. The Browns went 3-4 in his starts.

One line of thinking is that the Browns probably should determine once and for all what they have in Sanders, especially since they have two first-round picks ahead of the 2027 draft, which is expected to have a strong quarterback class. It's hard to do that when he's sitting on the bench.

But Monken is a first-year head coach who wants to make a strong initial impression, and picking the veteran quarterback is normally the safer bet. The issue in this case is that Watson has never been good in Cleveland and was awful in his second preseason appearance. Choosing him as the starter certainly feels like a predetermined choice.

Regardless, the pecking order has been set. Nobody will be surprised if Sanders ultimately takes over as the starter at some point in the regular season, however.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Picks in 2-Round Mock Draft and Top Keeper Rankings Advice
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL season nearing its opening kick, it's almost keeper-submission time for fantasy football managers.

While your specific league may require you to weigh thinks like draft-round or salary-cap costs, the general goal is keeping as much talent as possible.

It isn't always as simple as it sounds, though, so you might have come here seeking a few road signs to take you to title town. That's exactly what we have here in the form of a two-round mock draft, dynasty rankings and keeper advice.

This might be the most obvious advice you will hear, but it's also the most important. Because each keeper league has its own set of rules, you need to know exactly what they are, so you can apply them to the general advice you'll find in a place like this.

Universal rankings can be helpful, but they may not settle your debates. If your league uses a salary cap or attaches draft-pick costs to keepers, that changes things a lot. That third-round sleeper you found last season may not look as appealing this year if they jump to a second- or even first-round cost, for instance.

If you keep a big chunk of your roster, then you should have a pretty decent idea of your championship chances this season. Use those odds—the realistic ones, not the optimistic ones that only exist in a best-case scenario—to steer your draft decisions.

Win-right-now rosters need instant-impact, so you'd want to prioritize proven veterans over dart-throw rookies. Long-term rebuilders, on the other hand, have no use for 30-somethings, but they should be collecting as many long-term lottery tickets as possible. It only takes one jackpot prize or two to instantly change your team's trajectory.

Last year, Austin recorded 372 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.

Austin was expected to be the starting slot receiver for the Giants this year, but his injury on Tuesday means New York might have to find someone else to fill that role in the meantime. With Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton starting on the outside, the Giants could pivot to Braxton Berrios in the slot.

With Odell Beckham Jr. still looking for a permanent spot on the Giants, the veteran receiver could be in the mix to take over Austin's role.

Unfortunately for Austin, a significant injury would only add to what has been an injury-filled start to his career. Drafted in the fourth round in 2022, he missed all of his rookie season because of a lingering foot injury that he suffered in training camp.

articles.title: Dolly Partonâs final message to Travis Kelce is breaking hearts after her death
articles.summary: NFL News: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she \"died peacefully today in Nashville\" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, an.
articles.body: Dolly Parton has died at 80. Her family confirmed she "died peacefully today in Nashville" after dealing with health issues for the past few years, and no cause of death has been shared yet. And one of her last public moments with Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift is hitting harder now. This one clip, from just weeks ago, where she made a joke about wanting Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's future baby, is doing the rounds for a different reason now.When Dolly Parton joked she wanted Travis Kelce's firstborn, and why that memory now hits so hardBack in early July, Kelce and Swift donated $2 million to Dolly's Imagination Library, as part of a $26 million round of giving to charities tied to cities that mattered to them, announced right before their Madison Square Garden wedding.Dolly didn't just thank them quietly. She filmed a video, saying, "Taylor and Travis, it's Dolly, and I was just told that you two are making a donation of two million dollars to my Imagination Library. Thank you, thank you, thank you," before turning the moment into pure Dolly comedy, joking she wanted their firstborn because "that is gonna be one special baby." Then she sang "I Will Always Love You" straight into the camera, aimed right at them.It was funny then. It's something else entirely now. A woman who spent her whole life turning warmth into a punchline, gifting one more piece of herself to a couple she'd probably never met in person, that's the kind of thing you don't get to see twice.Remembering Dolly, beyond the jokeShe started out singing in church, was on local radio and TV by 13, and made her Grand Ole Opry debut around that same age, where she met Johnny Cash. From there she built one of the great crossover careers in music, releasing dozens of albums and winning 11 Grammys.But the Imagination Library, the same program Kelce and Swift just backed, was always the part of her legacy that felt closest to her heart. It wasn't about the music. It was about kids she'd never meet, getting books they'd never have gotten otherwise.Her family has asked that, instead of flowers, donations go to that same Imagination Library. Fitting, really. Even her goodbye is pointed at the same thing that clip was about - kids, books, and a kind of love that outlasts the person giving it.Kelce and Swift's $2 million didn't just fund a program. Las Vegas Raiders fans looking for clarity on the severity of Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury didn't get much from head coach Klint Kubiak on Tuesday.

"I'm not gonna get into the injuries," Kubiak told reporters when asked about the running back. "He's on the mend."

He also said , "Ashton got hurt in practice and the whole team took a knee. I think that says a lot about him being on the mend and us counting on him. So, really excited to get him back."

The comments come after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that Jeanty seemed to have avoided a season-ending injury.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

There was significant concern for Jeanty in the immediate aftermath of his setback, especially since Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post reported he couldn't put weight on his leg as he exited the field.

Yet ESPN's Adam Schefter and Rapoport reported it wasn't seen as "a long-term injury" even though there was still some uncertainty regarding the exact timeline.

Considering how secretive some NFL coaches are when it comes to injury updates, Kubiak's comments aren't surprising. He and the Raiders also may not know exactly when the running back will be ready to return to the field at this point.

Las Vegas starts the 2026 campaign on Sept. 13 against the Miami Dolphins.

Jeanty figures to be a major part of its offensive attack after he ran for 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie. The Raiders selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft with the hope he would become a franchise building block, and the 2026 campaign represents a chance for him to take a second-year leap.

He has to be on the field to do that, though, which makes the timing of his setback rather concerning even if it isn't a season-ending one.

If Jeanty is out for the game against the Dolphins, look for the Raiders to turn to Mike Washington Jr. at running back.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes says he feels 'great,' still hoping to play in Week 1
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has apparently hit the most optimistic deadlines during his ACL recovery.
articles.body:
When Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes went down with an ACL injury last December, the quarterback seemed likely to miss time early next season. While a quick ACL recovery wasn't necessarily unprecedented, it was rare.

With a few weeks to go before the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, Mahomes said he feels "great" and is still hopeful he'll be able to start in Week 1.

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7 — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) August 25, 2026

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7

Mahomes said he was initially told it would take nine months to recover from his injury. The quarterback underwent surgery Dec. 16, making Sept. 16 exactly nine months since his surgery. The Chiefs are slated to take on the Denver Broncos in Week 1 on Sept. 14, two days before the actual nine-month mark.

That's an aggressive timeline, but one Mahomes said he was always planning to hit.

"This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

While that's an encouraging update — as is the fact that Mahomes has been able to take part in team practices — the star quarterback has yet to be cleared to play in games just yet. If that doesn't happen by Friday, Mahomes would miss the entire NFL preseason for the first time in his career.

Even in that case, Mahomes would still have two more weeks to be cleared by team doctors.

In a league where careers and playoff hopes turn on exactly this kind of moment, that clip was enough to send an entire fanbase into a spiral before a single official word came out. Then, just as fast as the panic built, Chase himself picked up a mic and tried to shut it all down. Here's the full arc, from scare to relief, and why it's still worth reading the fine print.JaâMarr Chaseâs scary injury had Bengals fans fearing the worst Chase went up for a deep route against teammate DJ Turner at Tuesday's practice, landed awkwardly, and immediately grabbed his left knee. Video of the moment spread fast, Chase limping, trainers rushing over, head athletic trainer Matt Summers examining him for several minutes on the field.For a team about to open its season, and a receiver who just signed a four-year, $161 million extension in March, that's the kind of clip that sends fanbases spiraling before anyone's said a word officially.Here's the thing, even in the moment, this didn't look like a disaster. Chase walked off under his own power. His limp reportedly eased up as the day went on. He stayed on the practice field afterward instead of heading straight to the locker room, and was seen casually talking with Joe Burrow and DJ Turner not long after. None of that screams "serious injury." But screenshots of a guy grabbing his knee travel faster than context does, so the panic had already set in online before those details caught up.Chase himself is saying it's nothingSpeaking on ESPN 1530 with Tony Pike and Mo Egger, Chase called it a mild hyperextension and said he could have kept playing if it had been a real game. Straight from the source, that's about as reassuring as it gets.That said, worth flagging that this is Chase's own read on his own knee, on a radio hit, not an official Bengals medical statement or an MRI result. Players downplay injuries all the time, sometimes because that's genuinely how it feels, sometimes because nobody wants to hand the rest of the league bulletin-board material before Week 1. The Bengals themselves haven't put out an official statement on severity, so until there's a practice report or a coach's presser confirming Chase is full-go, "hyperextension, no big deal" is Chase's word, not a diagnosis.Best case: this really was a scare and nothing more, and Chase is back to full practice reps within days. Worst case: hyperextensions can still linger even when a guy insists he's fine. Bengals fans have been burned by exactly this pattern before with Chase's past hip and shoulder injuries, where "day-to-day" turned into multiple missed games. For now, take the good news, but keep one eye on the practice report before fully exhaling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The fragile, shaky, not-yet-feelgood story of Tua Tagovailoa's next act
articles.summary: Atlanta has two quarterbacks and one big problem: Can either stay healthy?
articles.body:
Walk very gently around the Falcons ' practice fields in Flowery Branch, Georgia. You might injure a quarterback.

Yes, while Cleveland is the site of the most controversial and misbegotten quarterback situation , Atlanta is home to the most delicate. Two oft-injured quarterbacks, Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., are ever-so-carefully competing for the starting job like they're trying to run across a hockey rink.

Penix, who partially tore his ACL last November, finally received clearance to begin full 11-on-11 work on Monday, meaning the Falcons' QB competition can now begin in earnest. Good thing, too, because the regular-season opener is coming up fast, and it's probably a good idea to have a starting QB in place at that point.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

The Falcons snagged Tagovailoa for the NFL equivalent of a scratch-and-dent bargain — one year, $1.2 million — as a combination insurance policy/camp challenge for Penix. This marks a clear new chapter for Tagovailoa, who first came to prominence at Alabama, throwing the famous second-and-26 national championship-winning pass against Georgia in the same building the Falcons call home. After going to Miami in the pandemic draft, where he sported a spectacular suit in his parents' home, Tagovailoa strung together six occasionally transcendent, often maddening injury-pocked seasons.

Tagovailoa occupies a strangely sympathetic position in the modern NFL. No other quarterback has suffered so much, so visibly in this decade, with at least four documented head injuries, along with an assortment of other health woes. A not-insignificant contingent of NFL fandom and commentators has called on Tagovailoa to retire — not because he's hurting the team, which is usually the reason for these calls, but out of fear he's hurting himself and jeopardizing his future.

A newly-released study which states that 25 percent of recently deceased NFL players had CTE is a stark reminder that head trauma remains a concern for NFL players, if not necessarily a headline-worthy news item. And if you're making a list of known head trauma victims now playing in the NFL, well, Tagovailoa tops the list, and there's no close second.

The head injuries alone are enough to proceed with caution on Tagovailoa, but this is a guy who's sustained shots all over his body — back, shoulder, knee, hip, ankle, throwing hand, foot, ribs. Point to a spot between the top of your head and the soles of your feet, and Tagovailoa has probably lost games after injuring it. He's been carted off fields all over the country, wearing both Alabama crimson and Miami teal. Even though he's now in Falcon red-and-black, the questions persist: How much more can he take of this?

For his part, Tagovailoa leans heavily on his faith to guide him through one of the more agonizing journeys in the NFL right now. "Outside of being able to feel centered, it also gives me a lot of perspective on life, what's important in life," he said recently at training camp. "Football is just what we do. It's not who we are."

After missing time early in the preseason with a tight back, Tagovailoa has been taking first-team reps while Penix heals. The results have looked good in practice, not so good in the first preseason game against Denver — 3-for-5 for 22 yards, with just one first down in two offensive series. He's never had a big arm, and he hasn't unleashed it with any regularity in a Falcons uniform, either.

"You have to make use of every opportunity you have, and that's not what we did," Tagovailoa said after the Broncos game, via The Athletic . "Definitely not up to standard. I have to be better for our guys."

"He's getting better every day," Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt insisted recently, per the team's website . "I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and the play-calls and protection adjustments and everything."

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is keeping his cards close on naming a starter, waiting to see how Penix performs in full-squad drills. But as with the ongoing scuffle in Cleveland, the fact that Tagovailoa hasn't yet seized the job for himself is at least a mild indictment in itself. (Tagovailoa did not play in the Falcons' second preseason game; no starters did.)

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

The Falcons backed themselves into this corner by drafting Penix just weeks after signing now-departed Kirk Cousins , and then watching as both went down with injuries and ineffectiveness. What should have been a position of excessive riches is now one of the largest question marks in the NFL.

For a team that's suffering through the longest playoff drought outside of the Jets — eight years and counting — the Falcons can't afford any more question marks. Atlanta needs answers, and fast. Still undetermined: whether Tagovailoa is the one to provide them.

articles.title: At least 25% of ex-NFL players who died from 2016-2021 had CTE, according to new study; NFLPA says findings should be 'a call to action across the entire football ecosystem'
articles.summary: The study used brain samples from the UNITE Brain Bank at Boston University.
articles.body:
A new study of NFL players who had played in at least one of the league's games and died between 2016-2021 showed at least 25% of them had CTE.

The study from researchers at Mass General Brigham — published Tuesday in The British Medical Journal — deepens the link between the head impacts NFL players suffer and chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the degenerative brain disease known as CTE.

"We've known that this disease process can be caused by, in part, repeated traumatic brain injury. But we didn't know how common it was," said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, lead author of the study, according to NPR .

The study used brain samples from the UNITE Brain Bank at Boston University, where the brains of more than 330 players who died from 2008-2021 have been donated. Researchers tested the brains of 235 of the 878 players who died from 2016-2021 for CTE. They found the disease in 215 of them.

Mood swings, memory loss and confusion are among the symptoms of CTE.

The NFL "continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league said in a statement to NPR.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing. We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

In response to the study's release, the NFL Players Association, according to Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio , sent its membership an email Tuesday acknowledging the data:

"These findings should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem. We all share a responsibility to advance research, improve access to care, develop better treatments, and support those affected by the long-term impacts of the game. While we have learned a great deal over the past two decades, there is more work to do."

The study's authors said the 25% estimate is likely low, not accounting for deceased players whose brains were not tested.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Gives Week 1 Injury Status Update Amid Knee Rehab as Chiefs Prepare for Broncos
articles.summary: There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.

Patrick Mahomes told reporters Tuesday he feels like he is on track to start in Week 1 as he continues his recovery from the torn ACL and LCL that ended his 2025 season.

"Being able to go out there, day after day, and have the grind of a camp, that can even be harder than the [regular] season," Mahomes said. "It's been awesome for me to be able to do that. It's exciting. I didn't know if I was going to have to take days off, but my body has responded the right way.

"Honestly, the more we practice, the better I feel."

While he has not played in a preseason game and is not expected to in Friday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, Mahomes has not missed practice since he was cleared to participate in football activities in July.

And, in his eyes, the timeline is matching up exactly as he expected.

"It's nine months," Mahomes said of the Week 1 start date. "It's the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week 1. I'm someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right.

"This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

This will be the first time in Mahomes' career that he doesn't play in a single preseason game, but the Chiefs know what they are getting in their star quarterback if he is healthy and available.

His resume includes three Super Bowl titles, three Super Bowl MVPs, two league MVPs, six Pro Bowl selections and six seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards. He led the league in both passing yards (5,250) and passing touchdowns (41) in 2022 and is already considered one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history.

It seems like he will have the opportunity to add to that resume this season given his progress from last year's injury.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan breaks 49ers silence on Jed York arrest, says he still has 'respect' for the club owner
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan says Jed York's arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting has no effect on the San Francisco 49ers as a team heading into the season.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers said they weren't going to comment about owner Jed York getting caught up in a prostitution sting over the weekend because the legal matter is closed , but that policy collapsed in coach Kyle Shanahan's first press conference since the incident. Shanahan became the first 49ers official to face questions, and he felt obliged to provide answers. (Dude is a saint). Shanahan said York's arrest and ensuing no-contest plea to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools charges in a deal with an Ohio prosecutor has no effect on the Bay Area football team. MORE DETAILS EMERGE ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN PROSTITUTION STING "My view is, as the coach, does it have effect on us as a team?" Shanahan said. "And that's what I continue to answer on from a football standpoint. It has no effect on us. I mean, as far as what we do day to day, what we talk about, it hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today. It doesn't have to do with what happens on the field." Shanahan, who was involved in a head-on collision in July that affected how much he was on the field early in training camp, doesn't believe that or York's legal trouble will distract the football team in the upcoming season. "Well, the one thing that went on yesterday I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team. "So I think it's been training camp as usual." 49ERS COACH KYLE SHANAHAN ADMITS HE CAUSED CAR CRASH AFTER TAKING EYES OFF ROAD TO FIND HIS PHONE This, of course, is a head coach's spin on an uncomfortable situation. The majority owner of the team spent a day in jail and was splashed across national headlines because, police documents say, he went on a website in Ohio and tried to enlist the services of a prostitute on Sunday. Three times. And he got caught because what he was actually doing was connecting with an operation run by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which arrested him with the help of East Palestine police. NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK Despite those details, Shanahan said he has not changed his opinion about the club's owner or his family. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan admitted after saying he has spoken to York the last two days. "I mean, the views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. "But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it being a personal [matter], I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way." Danielle Belluomini is York's wife of 15 years, but even the marriage has become a newsworthy drama. Multiple reports have cited a divorce petition filed by York almost four months ago with the reason for the break being "irreconcilable differences." NFL owners are scheduled to gather on Wednesday to vote on the sale of the Seattle Seahawks and the York situation will almost definitely be discussed in some capacity. The league released a statement on Monday saying it is aware of York's situation, and he is subject to discipline under its Personal Conduct Policy. So, whether Shanahan admits it or not, the football team could be affected if York is disciplined and that rises to a suspension or even removal — the latter of which is not likely but cannot be ruled out. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP None of that is a concern right now for the coach, and he believes his players aren't moved by the publicity of York's troubles. "That's what these guys deal with their whole careers," Shanahan said. "I got cameras on all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games, when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened. "I feel something like this is actually easier for them than some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle of things that are more personal to themselves." articles.title: Raiders pitch $158 million Allegiant Stadium upgrade with public money
articles.summary: With another Super Bowl on the horizon, the Las Vegas Raiders want to elevate its premier sports venue with a new multi-level event space aimed at tackling h...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are seeking approval for a $158 million upgrade to Allegiant Stadium 's north entrance, including $75 million in public funding. The proposal would add a larger arrival area with pedestrian and event decks, a public plaza, and transportation improvements around the stadium.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority considered the proposal at its August 20 meeting but did not vote on it. A vote could come September 2, with construction expected to begin after the Raiders' 2026 season. The project is being planned for completion in late 2028 or before the 2029 Super Bowl, which is scheduled to be held at Allegiant Stadium. NFL.com has more details on the proposal and funding plan .

New North Entrance Would Change the Arrival Experience

The proposed project centers on the north side of Allegiant Stadium, where large crowds currently converge after Raiders games and other major events.

The plans include an elevated pedestrian deck, an event deck, a public plaza and improvements to traffic and transportation access. A dedicated rideshare loop would sit beneath the second level, with the goal of making pickups and drop-offs more efficient.

Related: Popular rock band makes major change to Las Vegas Sphere residency

The new entrance would also provide a more direct connection from the Las Vegas Strip, with many fans currently using the nearby Hacienda Avenue bridge to reach the stadium.

Raiders president Sandra Douglass Morgan told the Stadium Authority that the north side has become a pressure point for the guest experience because the existing infrastructure is stretched to capacity.

How the $158 Million Project Would Be Funded

The Raiders are proposing that the Stadium Authority contribute up to $75 million, with the remaining cost covered by the team. The public portion would come from the waterfall residual fund, which is funded by room tax revenue.

The stadium itself opened in 2020 at a reported construction cost of about $2 billion. Public funding contributed to the original project totaled approximately $750 million.

The proposed improvements are intended to prepare the venue for the larger crowds and logistical demands that come with major sporting events and concerts. Allegiant Stadium hosted Super Bowl LVIII in 2024, and the venue is scheduled to host the 2028 Final Four as well as the 2029 Super Bowl.

For now, the project remains a proposal. The Stadium Authority did not take action on August 20, leaving a potential September 2 vote as the next major step.

The Raiders want construction to begin after the 2026 season, with completion targeted for late 2028 or earlier. A successful project would give one of Las Vegas' most prominent sports venues a significantly larger arrival area before it takes on another Super Bowl.

articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest
articles.summary: York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges, disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools, was sentenced to two days in jail and fined $1,150.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used the pseudonym "Joe" while responding to a fictitious ad on a prostitution website, leading to his Sunday morning arrest in a mobile home park located in East Palestine, Ohio, according to a Tuesday report from The Athletic .

York was charged with a pair of misdemeanors, initially including a prostitution charge that was eventually amended to disorderly conduct through a plea agreement, per ESPN . York's other charge was reportedly for possession of criminal tools, a classification that can apply to a cell phone. He pleaded no contest, was sentenced to two days in jail, one for each charge, and fined $1,150.

The Athletic, citing an incident report from the Mahoning Valley Law Enforcement Task Force, reported that police deployed an undercover advertisement, masquerading as a woman, to arrange a meeting with the 46-year-old York, who reportedly filed for divorce from his wife in May.

York contacted what he didn't know was an undercover officer twice on Saturday, according to ESPN , which also cited the incident report. The undercover officer reportedly didn't respond to York until Sunday, when York sent a third message.

York, a Youngstown, Ohio, native, messaged at 9:11 a.m. ET that he was driving in from nearby Boardman, per The Athletic. The two sides reportedly agreed on one hour of "full service sexual activity" for $160, and York was provided a fake lot number in East Palestine mobile home park, identified as the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in ESPN's report.

As reported by The Athletic, York was seen driving a rental car into the mobile home park and then back out to the main road after he couldn't find the made-up lot number. That's where he was reportedly stopped by police, who took York's phone and the $160 he planned to pay. That money was ultimately forfeited to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, according to The Athletic's report, but York's phone was returned.

York was named the 49ers' CEO in 2008. That's when he assumed day-to-day control of the team from his parents. In 2024, he purchased enough equity from his family to take over as the organization's principal owner.

Under York's supervision, San Francisco has reached the Super Bowl three times, although the franchise is still searching for its first ring since the 1994 season.

"As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the 49ers said in a statement regarding York's arrest.

The incident will be reviewed under the NFL's personal conduct policy, a league spokesperson said in a statement, according to multiple outlets.

Notably, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft didn't face punishment from the NFL after he was accused of paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. However, the charges against Kraft, misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution, were dropped.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Honored by Sports World After Country Music Legend Dies at 80
articles.summary: The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.

Dolly Parton died at 80, her nephew, Bryan Seaver, announced on Instagram.

Following Parton's death, the sports world honored the singer, whose impact stretched well beyond just her music.

Parton's music career spanned nearly 60 years, and she is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, with hits like "I Will Always Love You," "9-5" and "Jolene."

She was born in Sevier County, Tennessee, and went on to become arguably the most famous East Tennessean. She released her first album, "Hello, I'm Dolly," in 1967 and released 48 more solo studio albums, her final being "Rockstar" in 2023.

But Parton's music was just a portion of her extraordinary life.

She opened the Dollywood theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, in 1986, and the park has since become one of the most visited theme parks in the country. As part of the Dollywood Company, she also opened other attractions in the area, like the Dream More Resort and Spa and Dolly Parton's Stampede.

While her philanthropic efforts are immeasurable, Parton's Imagination Library is perhaps the most notable. The program began gifting free books to children in East Tennessee but has since stretched worldwide. Approximately one in six children under the age of five in the United States receives an Imagination Library Book each year.

Parton was a lifelong Tennessee fan and appeared at the Vols' 2023 game against Georgia to perform "Rocky Top," escorted onto the field by legendary quarterback Peyton Manning.

Parton had revealed on social media over the past year that her health began declining in March 2025 following the death of her husband, Carl Dean, with the most recent update coming last week.

articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Texted Woman He Believed Was a Prostitute Before His Arrest in Police Sting
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.

The report from the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force had more than two pages redacted but provided more details about what led to York's arrest and ultimately to him pleading no contest Monday to two misdemeanors.

York initially responded to an advertisement placed by police on a known prostitution website on Saturday, according to the report, sending two messages that went unanswered and saying his name was "Joe" and that he wanted to visit the woman.

49ers Owner Pleads No Contest to Misdemeanor Charges (AP)

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

York texted again Sunday morning and said he wanted to see the woman. He said he was staying nearby and asked for her address. He asked how much the woman charged and was told it was $160 for "full service sexual activity," the report said.

York took a rental car to a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio, where he was given a fictitious lot number. He texted when he arrived at the mobile home park. He was then directed back to the main road, where he was stopped by marked police units. Police found York had $160 that was seized and they sent a text to his phone to determine it was the same one used to arrange the meeting.

He was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest Monday to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the ad.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. The $160 that was seized from him was given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.

York has been in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown, for most of the summer. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league is aware of the arrest and will review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the policy.

The team said that the "legal matter" had been resolved and that it would have no additional comment.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that he has talked to York the past two days and doesn't believe the arrest will have any impact on the team.

"Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan said. "The views for the organization going forward are the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got lot of respect for Danielle. The family does mean a lot to me. With it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way."

Shanahan said he doesn't expect any change in York's involvement with the team, saying he has always allowed Shanahan and general manager John Lynch to make the football decisions.

Shanahan said he doesn't feel the need to address the situation with his players.

Star linebacker Fred Warner said the players were aware of it but that he didn't believe it would be a distraction.

"We all have social media, so we see things," he said. "But at the same time, I got a lot of love, a lot respect for Jed, and don't feel the need to comment on the situation. I think the team is kind of the same way. It really wasn't a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but at the time, we were so hyper-focused in this building of trying to prepare for Week 1. A lot of guys are on the bubble trying to make the team. So we're just trying to get better as a football team and that's a personal situation, and letting it stay personal with him."

articles.body: The NFL continues to make a concerted effort for safe play for all players, especially when it comes to head injuries. But since chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, was found to be heavily linked to former professional football players, there has been ongoing discussion about how current and future NFL players could be affected. The study found that at least one in every four people who have played in the NFL might expect to end up with CTE at some point in their lives. For the study, 878 former NFL players who died from 2016-21, which varied from players in their 20s to their 80s and in between, at least 215 of them had CTE in some stage. That’s 24.5%, with the actual prevalence likely being higher considering there were 643 of those brains that were not examined. One of the main problems of the degenerative brain disease is that it can only be confirmed as a diagnosis post-death once the brain is examined. The neurodegenerative disease is caused by repeated blows to the head as well as severe head trauma. The symptoms found in those with CTE include memory loss, mood swings, erratic behavioral actions and more. While the disease was first found in boxers, it has become associated with football players in this modern era due to the repeated blows to the head sustained on every snap of the ball. It has, however, also been found in athletes participating in hockey, rugby and other sports. But its connection to football became public when beloved players like Junior Seau, Mike Webster, Frank Gifford and others were diagnosed with CTE after their deaths. Webster was dubbed "Patient Zero" after Dr. Bennet Omalu examined his brain and became the first to diagnose an NFL player with CTE, jump-starting a concussion crisis within the game. Dr. Julian Bailes, a neurosurgeon and chief medical advisor for Q-30 Sports Science, has spent decades studying the disease as well as concussion and repetitive subconcussive impacts. He helped pioneer the early investigation into CTE, being portrayed by Alec Baldwin in the popular film, "Concussion." He has also authored more than 300 publications and previously advised the NFL Players Association, NCAA and Pop Warner Football. Seeing this study, Dr. Bailes believes it "should be a call to action for everyone involved in football." SUPER BOWL CHAMPION STEVE MCMICHAEL, WHO DIED LAST YEAR, REVEALED TO HAVE CTE "We have made tremendous progress in recognizing and managing concussions, but the science increasingly tells us that diagnosed concussions are only part of the equation," Dr. Bailes said in a statement provided to OutKick. "Repetitive head impacts accumulated over years of play matter, and we need to bring the same urgency we’ve applied to understanding CTE to preventing and reducing the forces experienced by the brain in the first place. "That means continuing to advance rules, training, equipment and new approaches to brain protection at every level of the game. This should not be approached as an all or nothing assignment. The next frontier in athlete safety must be proactive brain protection." A simple proactive action would be eliminating repeated blows to the head, which researchers know prevents CTE. Obviously, the game of football would forever be changed and there’s much more complexities there, especially at the professional level. "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league told The Athletic in a statement. "The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being." Christian Gonzalez is certainly frustrated to have not reached an extension with the New England Patriots, but he said Tuesday that his focus is on the 2026 campaign.

"It's frustrating, but I'm focused on the season," Gonzalez told reporters about his contract situation. "I'm focused on here now."

He also was a bit noncommittal when asked whether the contract situation could impact his status for Week 1.

His comments come after Patriots executive vice president Eliot Wolf said the two sides are continuing to have talks about a new deal.

"Each side is trying to do what's right for them. Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed," he said . "We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done."

Gonzalez is entering the final year of his rookie deal, though the Patriots picked up his $18.1 million club option for the 2027 season.

Gonzalez is coming off a tremendous year in which he recorded 69 tackles and 10 pass breakups to earn his first Pro Bowl selection. With Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon resetting the market with a deal that pays him $33 million per year, Gonzalez figures to command a similar number as well.

articles.title: Best Players In The NFL: Is Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes Or Myles Garrett The Top Star?
articles.summary: Here are our top 10 players in the NFL ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body: We've ranked the top 10 players at the most important positions in the NFL. Now, it's time to find out who is the best player in the league entering the 2026 season. Several players have a reasonable claim to be considered the NFL's best player ahead of the new year. Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is the reigning MVP, while his new teammate, Myles Garrett, just broke the NFL's single-season record for the most sacks. There are also other quarterbacks to consider, like Josh Allen. The Buffalo Bills star has consistently played at an elite level since the turn of the decade and won MVP in 2024. Of course, there's also Patrick Mahomes, who has widely been viewed as the NFL's best player for several years. So, who is the NFL's best player ahead of the 2026 season? Here are our top 10 players in the league. 10. LB Micah ParsonsGreen Bay Packers Ben Arthur: We’ll have to wait to see Parsons this year, as he’s expected to miss at least the first few games of the season recovering from an ACL tear. But a healthy Parsons is one of the NFL’s best players — a complete edge rusher with speed that elicits fear from opposing offensive linemen. Despite missing three games in 2025, he still registered 12.5 sacks and 81 pressures in his debut season with the Green Bay Packers en route to Pro Bowl honors. The former first-round pick has recorded at least 12 sacks in each of his five NFL seasons. The quicker Parsons returns to form, the faster the Packers become a Super Bowl contender. He’s that much of a force multiplier on defense. 9. OT Penei SewellDetroit Lions Greg Auman: Sewell is the oddsmakers’ favorite to win the Protector of the Year award, given to the NFL’s top offensive lineman, and he’ll do that as he tries to shift from right tackle to a new home at left tackle. It’s the same move the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Tristan Wirfs has made successfully, and if it takes, it solidifies Sewell at the top of his position. Sewell has four straight Pro Bowls, three straight first-team All-Pro nods and he’s still only 25 years old. We didn’t rank offensive linemen in our individual position rankings, so he’s making the overall top 10 here much like a write-in candidate, showing the strength of his value at his position. 8. DE Will Anderson Jr.Houston Texans Auman: What’s it like to be the best player on the best defense in the NFL? Anderson already has 30 sacks in three years and he hasn’t turned 25 yet. Give Houston credit. The Texans gave up a 2024 first-rounder and more to move all the way up from 12 to 3 to grab Anderson in the 2023 draft. Anderson and Danielle Hunter are one of the most dangerous edge-rush pairs in the league, and Anderson’s even better in the playoffs. He's got eight career sacks in six playoff games, with three forced fumbles in two playoff games last year. As Houston’s offense improves and they lead late in games more often, don’t be surprised if he takes another step to the 15-plus sack level in 2026. 7. RB Bijan RobinsonAtlanta Falcons Vacchiano: Here’s the crazy thing about the Atlanta Falcons running back: He had a combined 2,298 yards from scrimmage last season (1,478 rushing, 820 receiving) with 11 touchdowns and he touched the ball 366 times — 21.5 times per game. And there were still times he felt underused in the Falcons’ offense. It’s probably too much to ask new coach Kevin Stefanski to use him more, but it’s a good bet he’ll use him better. Robinson, still only 24 and entering his fourth NFL season, will have to be the workhorse in Atlanta as the Falcons sort through their quarterback mess, but Stefanski will surely find more creative ways to use him and get him into open space, where his moves, acceleration and breakaway speed make him one of the most dangerous weapons in the league. With his rushing ability and his receiving skills, he’s the closest thing the NFL has to Christian McCaffrey in his prime. And if the Falcons were ever good again, he’d be in the chase for MVP. 6. WR Jaxon Smith-NjigbaSeattle Seahawks Eric D. Williams: One of the best route runners in the league, Smith-Njigba showed he’s much more than a slot receiver in 2025. With DK Metcalf and Tyler Lockett no longer on the roster, Smith-Njigba leveled up, engineering one of his best seasons as a pro. Just 24 years old, the Ohio State product set franchise single-season records for receptions (119) and receiving yards (1,793) last season, taking home the league’s Offensive Player of the Year award. The Seahawks rewarded Smith-Njigba by signing him to a lucrative contract extension that made him the highest-paid receiver in the league, with an annual salary of $42.15 million. With Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker Jr. signing with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency and a new offensive coordinator Brian Fluery, taking over for the departed Klint Kubiak (now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders), Smith-Njigba will be counted on to shoulder even more of the offense. Smith-Njigba accounted for 44% of Seattle’s receiving yards, the highest percentage by any player in the league. He led Seattle in receiving yards in 16 of 17 games this year, the most in a regular season in NFL history. 5. QB Matthew StaffordLos Angeles Rams Vacchiano: What Stafford did at his age in 2025 was just ridiculous, especially considering the season began with a mysterious back injury that threatened to derail everything. He threw for career-highs in yards (4,707) and touchdown passes (47) while tossing just eight interceptions — the fourth quarterback ever to throw for more than 45 touchdowns with fewer than 10 interceptions — and he did it all at age 37. And with the Rams still loaded, there’s no reason to think he’ll be any different at age 38. It helps that Stafford’s in a perfect system for his talents, but he brings plenty of skills. His arm is still remarkably strong; he’s got picture-perfect mechanics, and no one is better at placing throws in perfect spots for his receivers. Put his mind and arm together in the Sean McVay system and you’ve got a quarterback who could win a Super Bowl and make a run at becoming just the sixth player to ever win back-to-back MVPs. He just needs his body to hold up. 4. WR Ja'Marr ChaseCincinnati Bengals Arthur: Chase is the most dominant wide receiver in football today. After winning the receiving triple crown in 2024, the Cincinnati Bengals superstar again led the NFL in receptions last season (185). The 26-year-old has recorded at least 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first five NFL seasons. The fifth overall pick in 2021, Chase is a high-volume target who possesses a unique blend of speed and physicality. He’s ranked in the top two in yards after the catch in each of the last two seasons. He’s been a near-unstoppable force since entering the league despite facing constant double teams. 3. QB Patrick MahomesKansas City Chiefs Williams: Returning from season-ending knee surgery after a disappointing 6-11 campaign in 2025, Mahomes is under a lot of pressure to show last year was a fluke. Mahomes should benefit from the return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy and the addition of Kenneth Walker III, implementing a more bullish rushing attack to create more balance on offense. But the 30-year-old Mahomes also must get back to playing more efficient football, relying less on his legs to keep the chains moving and getting more from his receivers on the perimeter. Mahomes has the Super Bowl pedigree, appearing in the game five times and winning three of them. And at 30 years old, Mahomes remains one of the best at his position, with plenty of more years to chase more Lombardi trophies. Mahomes owns an astounding 17-4 record in the playoffs. 2. QB Josh AllenBuffalo Bills McKenna: Allen is football’s version of Atlas, putting the world on his shoulders. It’s been like that for a while now in Buffalo, with Allen being, by far, the only most notable player on offense — but honestly, on either side of the ball. Defensive tackle Ed Oliver, tackle Dion Dawkins and running back James Cook are really great players. But receiver? Tight end? Cornerback? Edge? There really hasn’t been a big and productive name since Stefon Diggs. And Diggs’ departure coincided with the widespread respect for Allen, because people began to see just how much the QB can do for his team. The only thing he hasn’t done, of course, is win a Super Bowl. If he does that, he’ll be the No. 1 guy on this list — and perhaps even for years to come. 1. DE Myles GarrettLos Angeles Rams Auman: Garrett was a unanimous Defensive Player of the Year winner last year with the Browns after setting the NFL single-season record with 23 sacks. The thing is, he had only four sacks in his last six games, so now, joining a loaded Rams front, could he break his own record? He got 23 sacks despite Browns opponents being ahead often enough that they only passed 487 times, third-fewest of any team. The Rams, ahead much more, had opponents throw 102 more times than the Browns’ opponents, so that’s a ton more sack opportunities for the NFL’s best. Could we see a non-QB, non-offensive NFL MVP? If Garrett has the first 25-sack season in league history and the Rams win the NFC West, he’d have a compelling case to make for that.

The ruling comes after Dae'Quan Wright, a tight end for the Cleveland Browns , announced his intentions to leave the NFL and join his previous head coach from a year ago, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

While college basketball has seen its fair share of similar instances, this was the first case in college football, with many more likely to pursue the option to return to college.

Although the Big Ten has been the first conference to ban former NFL players from playing in their conference, there is an expectation that the SEC will have similar talks regarding a ruling.

Following comments made by Bret Bielema last week, this could have notable repercussions for Illinois.

Former Illini wide receiver Hank Beatty and offensive lineman Melvin Priestly were prime candidates to return prior to the ruling.

Both would have been great additions to the roster this fall, but as it stands, the Illinois roster appears to be set ahead of its season opener on September 3rd against UAB.

At a time when college athletics is akin to the Wild West, a ruling such as this provides a rare win for the NCAA to create a more stable league.

While NFL free agency is ongoing until the end of the Super Bowl, the Cleveland Browns and the rest of the NFL are mostly scraping the bottom of the barrel at this point in time in the season. Sure, RB Kareem Hunt might be able to help a team like the Detroit Lions , and the Browns are hoping that DE Derek Barnett helps offset the loss of DE Alex Wright , but there are reasons that players are still available on the NFL free-agent market.

NFL trade rumors could start to swirl as teams prepare for cutdown day, with Cleveland's Thursday Night contest giving them a bit of a head start . If the free agent market doesn't have answers, teams may look to swap positions of depth to help fill positions of weakness before starting preparation for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season.

A look at a 53-man roster projection for the Browns seems to indicate some obvious holes that could be filled on the trade market. Three positions stand out with depth concerns:

Harold Fannin Jr. is a great young starting point, but after that, Cleveland is looking at a career journeyman ( Blake Whiteheart ) and a late-round rookie ( Carsen Ryan ) to fill the rest of the depth chart. The NFL is not full of a lot of tight ends ready to play meaningful snaps who are also available in a trade, but GM Andrew Berry will likely make some calls.

Berry has been looking for edge help since training camp started, with Barnett coming in to offset Wright's injury. Any and every defensive end that could hit the waiver wire or free agent market might instead end up on the Browns roster via a trade.

With Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell , Cleveland's cornerback room is set at the top. The Browns seem convinced that Myles Harden can handle the slot corner spot but, beyond that, there are a lot of questions. DC Mike Rutenberg could end up playing a lot of three safeties to offset the corner need if Berry can't bring in any help.
